Hey everyone and @SamsungIndia Story start from 23 April 2026 till today, I have been trapped in what feels like a complete service scam by Samsung’s authorized service centre in Dharampeth, Nagpur, Maharashtra.

I discovered a sudden issue in the 0.6x ultra-wide camera of my Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra. The phone was never dropped, never mishandled. After researching online, I found MANY users reporting the exact same issue with the new 50MP ultra-wide sensor. Reddit, YouTube, Samsung Community — same problem everywhere.

Because my device was out of warranty, the Dharampeth service centre immediately gave me a ₹4000 quotation instead of acknowledging a possible manufacturing defect.

After endless emails, Samsung support kept repeating: “You have to pay.”

Why should customers pay for Samsung’s hardware failure?

After getting exhausted, I posted on X on 26 April tagging Samsung Electronics India. Only then did they react. Customer Experience Manager Kajal contacted me, and after I shared proof from multiple users online, Samsung finally offered a 73% discount.

I accepted because I was mentally tired of fighting.

On 6 May, I submitted the device. On 7 May, I collected it after paying ₹1000.

Camera fixed?
YES.

New disaster?
BACK PANEL STARTED COMING OFF THE VERY NEXT MORNING.

I informed the service centre on WhatsApp. They ignored the messages.

Visited again on 11 May — they “fixed” it.

Two days later?
BACK PANEL AGAIN COMING OFF.

Visited again on 14 May — this time the behavior became shocking.

Instead of accepting poor repair quality, staff started accusing ME of removing the back panel with sharp objects. They checked the device and found ZERO evidence.

Then they saw BGMI installed.

And suddenly their excuse became:
“BGMI is a third-party app. Using third-party apps voids warranty and service.”

Imagine buying one of Samsung’s most powerful flagship phones and being told GAMING can void service support.

When I asked for a written denial letter, they REFUSED.

When I started recording for proof, they stopped answering questions and began ignoring me completely.

I had no option left except calling the police.

ONLY after police intervention did the entire attitude of the service centre change. Suddenly:
“We never denied service.”
“We are ready to repair.”

They even requested police officers to convince me to delete the videos I recorded.

After another repair attempt, they told me:
“Do not use BGMI for 12 hours.”

I followed everything they said.

Result?
BACK PANEL STARTED COMING OFF AGAIN.

Two Muslim women journalists on Thursday alleged that they were beaten by Delhi police personnel in South Delhi’s Saket police station. The two journalists said that a police team detained them and took them to the Saket police station, where they were assaulted.The journalists were on assignment to cover an event attended by Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, following which the assault occurred, the journalists alleged. 

The journalists Shaheen Khan and Nafessa Khan alleged that they were dragged by their hair upstairs and were met with brutish assault for approximately 40 mins. 

“They dragged us upstairs by our hair and brutally assaulted us there. When they became exhausted from beating us, they stopped to take a break.”  Journalist Shaheen Khan told FoEJ Media. 

Both the journalists further claimed that on learning about their Muslim identity, the assault was intensified. 

“When they found out that we were Muslims, she said, ‘You’re Muslim? Now I’ll beat you even more'” Shaheen said. 

“She told me, ‘You’re Muslim? I’ll hit you three or four more times.’ She then struck me so hard with a lathi that the injury is still swollen.”  Nafeesa added, showing her bruises to FoEJ Media. 

Revealing the start of the assault, Shaheen said, “I was standing downstairs, speaking to my family over the phone and informing them about what had happened. Meanwhile, a female police officer approached me and demanded that I hand over my phone. When I told her, ‘Please tell me what happened; whatever you need to discuss, we can discuss it here,’ she replied, ‘I have a different way of talking. We’ll talk upstairs.’” 

“Listen to the language she used. She said, ‘I have a different way of talking. I’ll speak to you upstairs.'” Shaheen highlighted.

“She snatched my phone and started slapping me,” she added. 

Both the journalists further alleged that they were refused to have water even when they were falling to grasp the air due to the continuous assault. 

“When we asked, ‘Ma’am, please give us some water,’ she replied, ‘We will beat you thirsty,'” Shaheen alleged.

“Nafeesa’s condition deteriorated, and she collapsed unconscious. I told them that she needed medical attention, but no one paid any heed,” she added. 

The incident occurred on Thursday morning when the Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Minister Rekha Gupta attended the inauguration of Max Smart Super Speciality Hospital in Saket. 

The journalist said that they had gone to cover the event; however, they were stopped by police and taken to Saket police station, where the assault was launched. 

In an official statement, DCP (South) Anant Mittal described the allegations as “factually incorrect and misleading.”

“Claims suggesting otherwise, including allegations of assault for asking questions to the Hon’ble Chief Minister, are totally false, misleading, and baseless. Citizens and social media users are advised to refrain from circulating unverified and misleading information,” read the statement.  

The police said that despite multiple requests and instructions to remove the vehicles and clear the route, they refused to remove them. text:
"They could have killed my son": Mother demands answers

A Montreal man was pepper-sprayed, kicked, dragged across the pavement,  and stabbed by a group of masked men near Place-des-Arts, an attack that  left him with a punctured and collapsed lung, broken ribs and severe  facial fractures.

A 24-year-old man is speaking out after a brutal attack by more  than ten men of colour near Place-des-Arts metro station in downtown  Montreal left him hospitalized with serious injuries.

For security reasons and out of fear of retaliation, Rebel News is protecting the identities of both the victim and his mother.

Montreal police confirmed that a robbery involving multiple  suspects occurred on August 26. According to police, the victim was  pepper-sprayed, beaten and stabbed with a sharp object.

The victim told Rebel News he had been with friends near the  metro when a group of roughly two dozen masked individuals appeared  nearby. He described them as dressed mostly in black and said, “They  were all wearing COVID masks to hide their faces.”

Later that night, he says the group approached him from behind.

“One of them put his hand on my shoulder. He pulled me around, and immediately I… I got hit in the face with pepper spray.”

What followed, according to the victim, was a prolonged and vicious beating.

“Then they started punching me, kicking me, and dragging me  along the ground by my bag,” he said. “During that, I was stabbed  several times in the chest area, in the back.”

One stab wound punctured his lung. “Air was going in and out through my back. And I didn’t even know I’d been stabbed.”

He says his lung later collapsed and doctors had to remove both  air and blood before reinflating it. He also reported broken ribs,  facial fractures and continuing problems with vision in his left eye.

His approximately $5,000 Louis Vuitton bag, phone, cards and keys were stolen. Perhaps most disturbing to the family is what allegedly happened around them.

“It affects me quite a bit,” the victim said after being asked  about bystanders and friends who did not intervene. “I would at least  have intervened.”

His mother remains shaken. “Oh my God! I was angry, I was devastated, and I was worried,” she said after seeing video of the attack.

Asked about safety in Montreal, her answer was unequivocal: “There is no safety in Montreal anymore.”

Police have told Rebel News that no arrests have been made so far.

text:
Illegal Infiltration & Fake Documentation:-A Real Case I Handled

Home Minister @AmitShah ji has held that the population of Muslims in India has increased due to illegal infiltration. Let me share a real case I personally handled about 5–6 years ago in Mumbai, one among many that reveal how deep this problem runs. Please do read to understand the rot.

1. The Client’s Request:- One evening after court hours, a Muslim gentleman known to me came to my office. He had given his premises in Govandi, Mumbai, on a leave and license agreement to a family of 6/7 people.
Even after the agreement expired, the family refused to vacate.

I perused his papers and assured him of appropriate legal action. He then asked if the matter could be resolved sooner than usual.
When I explained that such cases typically take little time, he hesitated and what he said next stunned me.

2. The Shocking Revelation :- He quietly said, “Sir, those tenants are not Indians, they are Bangladeshis.”

That single sentence changed everything. Two thoughts struck me instantly:
1. Why hadn’t he mentioned this earlier?
2. How did they even get valid Aadhaar and PAN cards as visible in the agreement?

3. The Investigation:- On examining the documents, everything looked perfectly legitimate; Aadhaar, PAN, ration card, even voter ID.
We filed RTIs, involved the local police, and began to dig deeper.

Gradually, the truth surfaced, the birth certificate forming the basis of all these documents was forged.

Using that single forged certificate from 1967, the accused had created a full legal identity for himself and his family, including Aadhaar, PAN, ration card, and voter ID.

4. A Web of Fraud:- It didn’t stop there. The man had used the same method to obtain documents for his wife and children. His son was even married to an Indian Muslim woman, effectively merging into the Indian population.

During the investigation, we uncovered an organized network, a full-fledged industry operating to regularize illegal immigrants by manufacturing fake Indian identities that pass every verification test.

5. The Larger Problem:-India’s diversity makes such infiltration even easier. People entering from Bangladesh, Pakistan, Myanmar, or Nepal often resemble locals making visual identification almost impossible.

Add to this the corruption that exists from border checkpoints to administrative offices, and you have a perfect ecosystem for illegal population growth.

In this very case, we found the involvement of certain officials, and shockingly, even a few lawyers.

6. A Moment That Exposed the Rot:- One of those lawyers, representing the Bangladeshi accused, told my Muslim junior,
“How can you do this? This is a matter of religion.”
My junior stood firm and warned him of a complaint before the Bar Council.

This single moment revealed how some individuals, blinded by religious or political motives, are actively protecting those who illegally enter and settle in India.

7. The Unanswered Question:- 
This wasn’t the only case, I have come across several similar ones.
Despite being aware of this menace for years, successive governments have failed to implement a robust national mechanism to identify and deport such individuals.

8. The Hope:- Now that the Home Minister himself has spoken openly about the issue, one can only hope it translates into real, concrete action. India needs a firm, technology-backed, corruption-proof mechanism to detect and remove non-Indians living here on forged documents.

Illegal infiltration is not just a demographic concern, it’s a threat to national integrity, law, and fairness. The time for acknowledgment is over.
The time for action has arrived.

AP Police impersonated the FBI

Subject: Request for Investigation - Andhra Pradesh Police Officer Identified “FBI” as Requesting Organization in X/Twitter Law-Enforcement Request Concerning a U.S. Citizen

To:
Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
The Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
@FBI @FBIDirectorKash @FBITampa @TheJusticeDept  
U.S. Department of Justice

Dear Director / Appropriate Federal Officials:

I am a United States citizen residing in the United States. I respectfully submit this complaint and request for review concerning an apparent misrepresentation of U.S. federal law-enforcement identity in connection with a social-media investigation initiated by the Andhra Pradesh Police in India.

I. Summary of the complaint

I recently received a notification from X Support concerning a law-enforcement request submitted to X regarding my X account.
The X communication initially stated that the request had been submitted by the “FBI.”

However, X subsequently provided an important correction. X expressly stated:

“However, this request did not come from the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)”

X further stated that the request actually came from the Andhra Pradesh Police and identified the submitting individual as:

Name: A V Bramham
Position: Inspector of Police
Organization entered by requester: FBI
Email: guntururbansp-ap@gov.in
Location: Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, India
Country: India

X further stated:
“it is unclear why the Andhra Pradesh Police wrote ‘FBI’ as the sender organization.”
I have preserved the X communication and can provide the original notification and screenshot as evidence.
II. Why I am requesting U.S. government review
I fully recognize that foreign law-enforcement agencies may communicate with U.S. companies through legitimate international law-enforcement cooperation channels.
The issue here is different.

According to X’s own records, an Andhra Pradesh Police official submitted the request, but the requesting organization was entered as “FBI.”

I therefore respectfully request that the appropriate U.S. authorities determine:

Whether the FBI had any involvement whatsoever in this request to X.

Whether any FBI office, agent, liaison officer, or other U.S. government agency authorized, participated in, or communicated with Andhra Pradesh Police concerning my X account.
Whether the Andhra Pradesh Police official knowingly or inadvertently represented himself or his agency as the FBI when submitting the request to X.

Whether the use of “FBI” as the requesting organization was intended to obtain greater credibility, priority, cooperation, disclosure, restriction, or removal of content from X.

Whether X received any other law-enforcement request from Andhra Pradesh Police concerning my account in which the FBI was similarly identified.

Whether this conduct implicates any U.S. federal criminal, civil-rights, cyber, impersonation, transnational-repression, or other federal jurisdiction.

Whether the conduct should be referred to another appropriate federal authority for investigation.
III. First Amendment / transnational-repression concern
The underlying matter concerns social-media content posted on X and alleged violations of Indian law.
I am particularly concerned because I am a U.S. citizen residing in the United States, and the governmental action concerns my online speech and political commentary.
I understand that the United States cannot simply disregard legitimate foreign criminal investigations. However, I am requesting that U.S. authorities determine whether a foreign law-enforcement agency has attempted to use the identity or authority of a U.S. federal agency to influence or restrict constitutionally protected activity occurring in the United States.
The FBI itself recognizes transnational repression as an issue that may affect people in the United States and specifically directs individuals who believe they have been affected by transnational repression to report the matter to the FBI.
IV. Request for preservation and investigation of evidence
I respectfully request that the appropriate agency consider preserving and/or obtaining, where legally appropriate:
the original law-enforcement request submitted by Andhra Pradesh Police to X;

all metadata associated with that request;

the identity and authentication information associated with the requester;

the date and time of submission;

all representations made by the requester concerning his identity and governmental organization;
any attachments, legal documents, FIRs, court orders, or other materials submitted to X;

any subsequent communications between X and Andhra Pradesh Police concerning my account;
any communications between U.S. government agencies and Andhra Pradesh Police concerning this matter; and
any evidence showing whether “FBI” was entered intentionally or accidentally.
V. Request for clarification from the FBI
I respectfully request confirmation of the following:
Did the FBI have any involvement in, authorization of, or knowledge of this particular request to X?
If the answer is no, I respectfully request that the FBI consider whether the circumstances warrant investigation or referral concerning the apparent use of the FBI’s identity by a foreign law-enforcement official.
VI. Good-faith submission
I am not asking the U.S. government to interfere with a legitimate Indian criminal investigation.
My request is narrower:
I am asking the United States government to determine whether an Indian police official represented himself or his agency as the FBI when submitting a law-enforcement request concerning a U.S. citizen’s social-media account, and whether that conduct violated any U.S. law or raised a transnational-repression or foreign-government intimidation concern.

I am prepared to provide the original X communication, screenshots, account information, relevant posts, and any notices received from Andhra Pradesh Police.

I respectfully request that this complaint be logged, reviewed, and referred to the appropriate federal authority if the receiving office does not have jurisdiction.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.
Respectfully,

U.S. Citizen

text:
IPS officer transferred in India over Islamic greeting in video

Indian Police Service officer Bushra Bano has been transferred from her post as additional superintendent of police, Kharagpur of West Bengal, India, after a Hindu rightwing group took offence at her using an Islamic greeting in a video encouraging students to prepare for civil services, reports The Wire.

On Sunday, Bushra had posted a video on X in which she spoke of the help she received at Aligarh Muslim University’s Residential Coaching Academy while preparing for the Union Public Service Commission exams.

She spoke about preparing for the exams after completing her PhD and returning from a teaching job in Saudi Arabia in the video.

She said that the resources, books, library materials, mock tests at the academy were very helpful in her preparation and urged other students to make use of them.

“I hope more students enroll at the academy and use this platform so that more people like me can come forward,” she said in her video.

Hindu Legal Fund, which describes itself as a unit of the Hindu Network Foundation, filed a complaint against Bano’s video with West Bengal home secretary, saying that she did not use phrases like Vande Mataram or Jai Hind and instead began her video with Assalamualaikum, The Wire says.

“She began with Assalamualaikum, used Inshallah, ended with Jazakallah and did not use Vande Mataram or Jai Hind. A serving officer representing the Indian state should maintain neutrality and use national expressions in public communication. Seeking appropriate review and action,” Hindu Legal Fund said in a post on X.

While some users on X criticised Bushra for using a religious greeting, many others were quick to point out the varying standards of religious neutrality applied to officials of different faiths.

“India’s true strength lies in its unity amidst diversity. Mashallah to Bushra Bano IPS, an officer who cleared the UPSC twice, left a comfortable job in Saudi Arabia, and is now serving the nation with complete dedication. Her choice of words reflects her personal faith, not a denial of the country she safeguards. In a vast and diverse nation like India, this coexistence is not a weakness, but our pride. Thank you for your service, Bushra! Jazakallah Khair!” former civil servant Ashish Joshi said in a post on X.

“Why is slogan of ‘JSR’ acceptable from HM #AmitShah, while ‘Assalamualykum’, a greeting wishing peace, invites scrutiny when spoken by a Muslim IPS officer? When neutrality is the rule in democracy, why isn’t it applied equally for all?” another X user asked.

text:
The Delhi Police's takedown drive against posts critical of the Prime Minister is unconstitutional. 

New Delhi, 27 July 2026

Media reports today state that the Delhi Police has directed social media platforms to remove posts, videos, memes and reels containing remarks it describes as "abusive", "offensive" and "objectionable" towards the Prime Minister, uploaded during the student protests at Jantar Mantar and after the 'Sansad Chalo' march of 20 July 2026. At least three platforms have reportedly received notices. Several posts have already been taken down. A dedicated police team is monitoring social media to identify further content, and reports indicate that criminal proceedings are contemplated against those who posted it. No order has been published. While reports indicate the notices invoke the Information Technology Act, the specific provision relied upon and the text of the notices remain undisclosed. 

The Internet Freedom Foundation condemns this takedown drive and calls for the notices to be disclosed and withdrawn.

On the reports available, the content being removed is political expression. The movement at Jantar Mantar has been conducted as much through reels, memes, posters and digital artwork as through assembly on the ground. This is how a digital native generation raised online speaks about accountability. As per Article 19(2) restrictions on speech only on eight specified grounds. Offensiveness is not one of them. In Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) 5 SCC 1, the Supreme Court struck down Section 66A of the IT Act precisely because expressions such as "grossly offensive" and causing "annoyance" were vague, subjective, and swept protected speech within their net. Eleven years later, the Delhi Police is applying the same standard through informal notices and legal powers which are not being publicly disclosed. 

As per existing practices there are two routes for removing online content. The first is Section 69A of the IT Act read with the Blocking Rules, 2009, which requires a reasoned order, committee review, and notice to the originator, as the Delhi High Court affirmed in Tanul Thakur v. Union of India (2022). The second is Section 79(3)(b), which Shreya Singhal read down to require a court order or a government notification strictly confined to Article 19(2) grounds. If these notices were routed through the Sahyog Portal, they rest on a regime whose constitutionality remains under challenge before multiple High Courts. However, even if it is used police notices citing offensiveness satisfy neither. 

Reports that platforms were told the content violates "their policies" make the defect worse, the police have no mandate to enforce the community guidelines of private companies. Unpublished directions are also contrary to Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020) 3 SCC 637, which requires that orders restricting fundamental rights be published so that they can be challenged. If the underlying theory is defamation of the Prime Minister, the police have no role at all. Defamation under Section 356 of the BNS is a non-cognizable offence, prosecuted only on a complaint by the person aggrieved under Section 222 of the BNSS. 

Our demands

1. The Delhi Police must publish every notice issued, the legal provision invoked, and the list of URLs affected.

2. Notices directed at satire, criticism, and political commentary must be withdrawn. Any removal must follow the procedures under Section 69A or a judicial order.

3. No criminal proceedings should be initiated against persons for speech that does not meet the constitutional threshold of incitement.

4. Platforms must decline requests unsupported by valid legal orders, notify affected users, and disclose the number of government demands in their transparency reports.

Students who question an examination system are exercising their fundamental rights and deleting their posts will not delete their questions.

Reports referred to:

1. Times of India, "Delhi Police orders removal of offensive posts against PM Narendra Modi linked to NEET paper leak protests", 27 July 2026
2. News18, "Delhi Police Issues Notices To Social Media Platforms Over Offensive Posts Against PM Modi During Jantar Mantar Protest", 27 July 2026

Towards Fast Disposal of Court Cases in India and Making Judiciary Accountable

with about five crore cases pending in courts and tribunals of this country, India perhaps may be on top in cases in courts and tribunals both in respect of total number of cases and even according to court-cases proportionate to population thus making a much larger number of families and individuals always involved in tense-filled costly litigations paving way for judicial corruption at all levels with even Madras High Court Confessing- None can deny there is corruption in judiciary, judges are not holy cows- with India ranking poorly at 86th place out of 143 countries in WJP Rule of Law Index. Corruption in Indian Judicial System is also a factor for India ranking poorly at 96th place out of 180 countries in Corruption Perception Index While ranking at 118th place out of total 147 countries in World Happiness Report

Fast disposal of cases in Indian courts and tribunals on lines of developed countries can to some extent can overcome the problem as highlighted here-above. Much of time in Indian courts is spent on long adjournments where petitioners go on seeking adjournment after adjournment after managing an ex-party stay-order on first day of hearing. Division Bench of Supreme Court comprising of Justices RV Ravindran and JM Panchal in January 2009 observed and rightly too of the bitter reality that at times those having taken ex-party stay-orders seeking frequent adjournments in most cases ultimately lose the cases. Adjournments may be given only in exceptional cases. Court-cases should be contested mainly on basis of written arguments rather than on basis of oral arguments so that no law-point may be missing from records while there are every chances that oral arguments may not be fully become part of court-verdicts. System will again avoid adjournment-culture where at many times adjournments are sought on basis of non-appearance of arguing lawyers due to various reasons. Such a system will make litigations less costly because of less need of costly senior-designated lawyers required for oral arguments. Rather system of having senior-designated lawyers should be abolished altogether.Modern technology can further add to reduction of court-cases. Cheque-bouncing cases filed under section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act can be drastically reduced by inserting a QR-code on every cheque where decoding of QR code may reveal complete details of cheques bounced from the bank-account/s may be available.

Another reason for such large number of court-cases is Perjury where it has become a usual tradition to speak lie in Indian courts and to file false affidavits with extremely low conviction-rate making wrong-doers worriless with no fear of law leading to a high crime-rate. Rajasthan High Court had to once direct action against two Oath Commissionershaving attested an affidavit while the applicant was out of the country. Such an illegal practice is quite common when usually Oath Commissioners and Notary Public fulfill formality of attesting documents without verifying the person or signature whose signatures are to be attested. Phenomenon of Oath-Commissioners and Notary Public where they usually charge fees much in excess than fixed by the government should be totally abolished. Instead power of attestation should be given to every registered lawyer. This will induce at least some accountability on lawyers too when they will be attesting for their clients. Power of attestation can also be given chartered-accountants, medical-practitioners, officers of government and public-sector-undertakings. Station-House-Officers (SHOs) of police-stations who presently do not have such powers, may be authorized and duty-bound to free-of-cost attest documents of those who do not have easy access to authorities mentioned above.

India is perhaps the only country where judges recommend to appoint judges in higher judiciary resulting in a constant tussle between legislature and judiciary. Collegium-system at Supreme Court for recommending appointments and transfers at Supreme Court and High Courts is also at times under criticism for some selected families observed as dominating Indian judiciary. It may also not be advisable to hand over appointment in higher judiciary solely in hands of political hands of legislature. A balanced approach can be achieved by instituting a high-powered National Judicial Commission having retired Supreme Court judges as member-nominees of President, Prime Minister, Leader of largest Opposition Party in Lok Sabha, Chief Justice of India (CJI) and Bar Council of India with Chief Vigilance Commissioner as ex-officio member of the Commission with Union Law Secretary as ex-officio member-secretary of such a Commission. CJI may head such a high-powered Commission. Recommendations of such a Commission should be final, and sent directly to President of India for a formal endorsement. Retirement-age of High Court judges should be raised to 65 years to be at par with that of Supreme Court judges to avoid any chances of lobbying for promotion as Supreme Court judges only because to be in system for three extra years. Reforms for future may be there to establish Indian Judicial Service (IJS) on lines of Indian Administrative Service (IAS) where those passing the tough competition may be appointed first at District Courts and ultimately to be elevated first to High Courts and then to Supreme Court.

To prevent chances of influencing locally appointed High Court judges either through their former bar-colleagues or local relations, all High Court judges should be compulsorily appointed outside from their home-states. To eliminate political bias in judiciary, it should be ensured that no person may be appointed as judge with an active political background. Even after retirement if any judge joins politics, he must lose all his post-retirement benefits. No judge should be given any post-retirement job anywhere after two years of retirement. It should be ensured that any person seated as CJI must get at least one year to be on post before he attains retirement-age of 65 years. Indian system is witness of contrast cases with Justice Kamal Narain Singh having been CJI for just 18 days (25.11.1991 to 12.12.1991) while Justice Yeshwant Vishnu Chandrachud having been CJI for more than seven years (22.02.1978 to 11.07.1985).

Suggested National Judicial Commission should also be empowered to probe all complaints against judges including Chief Justices of Supreme Court and High Courts, abolishing cumbersome and impractical system of removal of tainted judges through impeachment. It is noteworthy that in present system, there is no disciplinary authority for Chief Justice of India. Findings of the Commission and punishment suggested for such guilty-found judges should be endorsed for action with all post-retirement benefits of such tainted judges abolished. Even nothing could be done in the first-ever impeachment-case of Justice V Ramaswamy where the motion fell because of north-south divide of legislature. Tax-payers’ hard-earned money was wasted in paying a judge of a High Court for no work while on post and after retirement after the Supreme Court Collegium decided to recommend his impeachment. Judges are also human-beings picked up from the same society which has both honest and dishonest persons. Chairs of judges are not made from some divine material which can turn some undesirable one found entry as judge to turn fair.

Status of Chief Justice of India should be made at par with that of Union Cabinet Secretary, and of all other Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts at par with that Secretary in the Government in all respects of monetary and other benefits while on post and after retirement. However, for protocol purposes, Chief Justice of India and other Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts, existing position may be maintained. No extra-ordinary privileges should be provided to retired judges which presently also include life-time domestic help for them and their spouses after deaths of retired judges. Since pensions to government-employees has been done away, same system should be there for those in judiciary (and even in legislature).

All judges from Supreme Court to trial-courts must compulsorily record reason for recusal from the case on the file. Moreover, any such recusal should be informed immediately so that a new bench may be there for hearing without requiring any postponement of the hearing. A judge of Delhi High Court once recused herself from hearing a case where she herself issued notice to former President Pranab Mukerji after admitting a writ filed by some individual urging some contents of the book authored by the former President to be deleted. At times judges of higher courts have written to sitting Chief Justice of India about pressure and influence especially also from politicians. Making it compulsory to give reasons for recusal will prevent pressure and influence on judges.

Long summer vacations in courts were designed by erstwhile British rulers to save British judges in India from severe hot weather of this country, and also to facilitate them to visit their homeland. Unfortunately system continues in free India even after about eight long decades of independence, that too with long pendency of court-cases. Long-pending recommendation of Law Commission for scrapping long court-vacations should be implemented. Courts should adopt normal government-calendars for holidays abolishing system of week-long vacations for religious festivals apart from long winter and summer vacations.

Whole system of continuing naming High Courts is confusing where some High Courts are still named after cities where these are situated. Indian cities Bombay, Madras, Allahabad have since been renamed as Mumbai, Chennai and Prayag respectively long time back. But High Courts located in these cities are still officially named after old names of these cities. System should be that names of High Courts may get auto-changed with change in names of cities. Best is to end the British legacy by naming all High Courts after names of states rather than on cities. Proposed legislation should incorporate feature that names of High Courts may be automatically changed with change in name of states without needing any separate legislation.

text:
IFF statement against the Alarming Escalation of Social Media Censorship and Proposed Expansion of Takedown Powers

New Delhi, March 19, 2026

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) is concerned by continuing reports of posts and accounts being withheld in India on Facebook, X and Instagram, including satire and criticism of the government. Recent reporting shows users receiving generic “withheld in India” notices or emails under Section 69A from social media platforms, with little or no explanation, while independent reporting has documented takedowns affecting speech that appears political, satirical, or critical rather than clearly unlawful.

As reported by Business Standard and The Indian Express on March 18, the Union Government is currently exploring a proposal to decentralize content blocking powers under Section 69A of the IT Act. The new proposal would grant direct takedown powers to multiple ministries, including Defence, Home Affairs, External Affairs, and Information & Broadcasting. At present, MeitY signs off on Section 69A orders, while a separate notice and takedown channel already operates through Section 79(3)(b) and the Home Ministry led Sahyog portal that at least has 35 nodal officers across State Police Departments in India.

At the same time, the February 2026 amendments to the IT Rules have sharply compressed compliance timelines. MeitY’s own published FAQ says intermediaries must act within 3 hours when they receive actual knowledge through a court order or a government intimation, within 36 hours for certain expedited grievances, and within 2 hours for specified complaints involving nudity, sexual content, morphed content, and impersonation. The government has also reiterated that intermediaries which fail to observe due diligence risk losing Section 79 immunity. A system built on speed, legal threat, and secrecy predictably incentivises over compliance.

We remind the Union Government that the Supreme Court upheld Section 69A in the Shreya Singhal case on the basis of procedural safeguards and written reasons that could be challenged. Secret and inaccessible censorship defeats those safeguards in practice. 

IFF calls on the Union government to halt any move to decentralise Section 69A blocking powers further, publish blocking orders with only as per the letter and spirit of the Shreya Singhal judgement, and ensure timely notice to affected users with clear grounds and avenues for remedy. Platforms must also do more than send boilerplate messages. They should provide meaningful notice, preserve records for challenge, and publish granular transparency reporting given online censorship also impacts the public right to receive information.

If your account or post has been withheld or blocked in India, please write to legal@internetfreedom.in with screenshots, URLs, and any email or platform notice you have received. IFF will try to assist impacted users and document patterns of opaque censorship.

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

This issue may look small, but similar issues are happening everywhere, and no one is noticing them. It feels like “Kare koi aur bhare koi.” Many innocent people face this issue, and it remains unresolved. Because of chain transactions that come into accounts, some people are unable to use their own money. If I travel, I will have to spend more than 6000 rupees to remove the lien. I believe this issue can be resolved through email or online verification, but the investigation officer denied it.

I am also tagging Pushpendra Sir @pushpendrakum and Bangalore Cyber Police @BlrCityPolice . If you could please look into this matter.

Thank you.

Bhai aur beheno, agar aap bhi Binance P2P trading karte ho aur suddenly bank account freeze ho gaya hai toh pareshan mat ho. Yeh bahut common problem hai India mein. Innocent log bhi fas jaate hain jab kisi buyer/seller ka paisa kisi fraud case se link hota hai.

Yeh steps follow karo - 

1️⃣ Sabse Pehle Bank Branch Jaao  
   - Freeze ka exact reason, Cyber Crime complaint number, IO naam aur Police Station details lo.  
   - Written notice maang lo.

2️⃣ Saare Proofs Collect Karo (Bahut Important)  
   - Binance P2P complete order history (screenshots)  
   - Buyer/Seller ke saath chat  
   - Payment proof (UPI, bank transfer screenshot)  
   - Bank statement jisme transaction dikhe  
   - Aadhaar, PAN, Binance account details

3️⃣ Binance Support ko turant contact karo  
   - App mein Help section → Submit ticket  
   - Order ID aur proofs attach karo. Woh counterparty ko investigate kar sakte hain.

4️⃣ Cyber Cell mein Representation Daalo  
   - Local Cyber Police Station ya online portal pe jaao.  
   - Detailed application likho ki transaction genuine tha Binance P2P pe hua.  
   - Saare proofs attach karo.  
   - Lawyer (Cyber crime specialist) ki madad le lo - yeh bahut kaam aata hai.

5️⃣ Follow-up karte raho  
   - Har 7-10 din mein bank aur cyber cell ko call/email karo.  
   - Partial release ke liye request kar sakte ho.

• P2P ke liye alag dedicated bank account use karo (savings account mat use karo)

is the ECI compromised?  
 In March 2026, ahead of the Kerala Assembly elections (polling on 9 April 2026), a 2019 Election Commission of India (ECI) letter redistributed by the Kerala Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office was found to carry the seal of the BJP’s Kerala unit. This sparked a political row, followed by police-directed efforts to remove related social media posts

This takedown action itself became controversial, with critics framing it as an attempt to suppress discussion of an official lapse during an election period, while authorities maintained it was necessary to stop the circulation of a withdrawn and erroneous document that was being used to question the ECI’s credibility.The episode remained a flashpoint in the final stretch of the Kerala campaign, with the ECI treating it as a corrected administrative mistake and the opposition presenting it as evidence of deeper concerns about the poll body’s independence.The letter and the seal
The document was an ECI communication dated 19 March 2019 containing guidelines/FAQs on the publicity of candidates’ criminal antecedents (following a Supreme Court judgment). CPI(M) and Congress shared versions online showing the BJP Kerala unit’s seal. It had been circulated by the Kerala CEO’s office to political parties, District Election Officers, and Returning Officers as part of clarifications around mid-March 2026.thesouthfirst.comKerala CEO / ECI explanation:
It was described as a “purely clerical error.” The BJP Kerala unit had approached the CEO’s office seeking clarification on the (by then revised) 2019 guidelines and submitted a photocopy of the original directive that already bore the party’s seal. Staff overlooked this and redistributed that version. The error was identified; on 21 March a formal withdrawal notice was issued telling recipients to disregard the document. An Assistant Section Officer was suspended pending inquiry. Later, a Deputy CEO and a Section Officer were relieved of election-related duties.livemint.comOpposition parties (CPI(M) and Congress) rejected the clerical-error account. text:
Can we talk about Meta's glasses for a second?

They look like ordinary sunglasses, and the only warning is a tiny LED most people never notice. In just three weeks, we've sent two legal notices to Meta. One is for a man secretly filmed and mocked at a Delhi café. The other is for a woman covertly recorded on her walk home for a "pickup artist's" Instagram content.

Being in public shouldn't mean becoming someone's content without your consent. This is NOT normal.

Here are the two legal notices we sent to Meta over its Ray-Ban smart glasses:

Case 1: Harassment for clout
A man sitting alone at a café was harassed and secretly filmed, and the video was posted to mock him. We're seeking ₹2.05 crore in damages.
Read more: https://t.co/l8nJZDlX3w

Case 2: Stalking as "pickup" content
A woman walking home was covertly recorded to sell "approach classes" on Instagram. She filed a police complaint, and we sent Meta a second notice.
Read more: https://t.co/GXoD9IHFZd

If you've ever been filmed like this without your consent, you're not alone, and it's not okay. Please share this with someone who should know.

Phone jammers 👇🏽👇🏽

quotedTweet.text:
There is a crucial difference between an internet shutdown and a phone jammer. An internet shutdown requires a written order under the Telecommunications Act. A jammer is a radio transmitter that can cut voice calls, SMS and mobile data for everyone within its range. So who gives the Delhi Police the power to switch one on? (1/10)
Read More: https://t.co/kU0KOf2fOY

text:
There is a crucial difference between an internet shutdown and a phone jammer. An internet shutdown requires a written order under the Telecommunications Act. A jammer is a radio transmitter that can cut voice calls, SMS and mobile data for everyone within its range. So who gives the Delhi Police the power to switch one on? (1/10)
Read More: https://t.co/kU0KOf2fOY

On 8 September, IFF filed three RTIs with the Delhi Police. We are seeking records on every jammer it possesses, the permissions and procurement documents, the officers authorised to deploy them, the applicable SOPs and deployment registers, and the specific records concerning Jantar Mantar on 20 and 22 July. We have also asked for the records behind the Satya Niketan denial. (9/10)

The question is not whether telecommunications can ever be restricted. Indian law already provides a framework for temporary suspension of services. The question is whether a separate, less visible mechanism can bypass those safeguards and cut communications without the written order, publication, review and accountability that accompany a lawful shutdown. IFF will publish the Delhi Police's replies, including any silence, and continue seeking clarity on who can jam communications, for what purpose and under what law. (10/10)

Support our work: https://t.co/qSG7IzUpIX

This matters because the Delhi Police has powers to regulate public assemblies under the Delhi Police Act, and urgent powers exist under Section 163 of the BNSS. But neither provision gives the police a power to jam telecommunications. In *Anuradha Bhasin*, the Supreme Court held that telecommunications can be suspended only through the legally prescribed framework. Section 163 cannot become a substitute for that framework. (6/10)

There is also a basic rights problem. RML Hospital received injured police personnel after clashes near Jantar Mantar on 22 July, and RML and Lady Hardinge are within roughly two kilometres of the protest site. A jammer that cuts ordinary phone service can also cut a person's ability to call 112, a hospital or family. It can also prevent journalists and citizens from transmitting what is happening at a public assembly. (7/10)

Ray-Ban Meta glasses struck again. A woman walking home alone was secretly recorded by a man who approached her, then posted the footage on Instagram alongside similar clips of him doing this to other women, as part of "pickup" content.

She's filed a police complaint for stalking and voyeurism. IFF is assisting her with a legal notice to the creator, Instagram, and Meta, the second such notice against Meta in India.

This isn't a one off. It's a design problem.
Read more about it: https://t.co/x5Gzp2NFF0

A woman was followed, stopped on a dark street, secretly recorded through Ray-Ban Meta glasses and turned into an Instagram “pickup” reel that reached over 23 lakh views. Now, our legal notice seeks accountability from both him and Meta. (1/10)

Read More: https://t.co/x5Gzp2NFF0

The legal notice therefore puts Meta on notice not merely as the platform hosting the video, but as the designer, developer, manufacturer, marketer and seller of the glasses. It alleges negligence and product liability, arguing that Meta knew about the pattern of misuse but continued selling the device without an effective way for non-users or people being recorded to report that misuse. (9/10)

The notice seeks removal of every copy, preservation and disclosure of evidence, suspension of monetisation, an account of profits, an apology, and ₹2.05 crore in compensatory and exemplary damages. This case raises a larger question: when a company makes a camera that can be worn like ordinary glasses, who protects the person being recorded? Privacy cannot depend on whether the person being filmed has an Instagram account. (10/10)
